summary: Scheduled warmup rollback triggering sporadic 429s for multipart uploader
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasSearch reports intermittent 429 throttles affecting their multipart uploader after a scheduled warmup rollback ran on their dedicated pool. Throttles are observed primarily during large backfill batches that run multipart uploads in parallel.

Impact:
- Affects ~2% of uploader requests during backfill windows, causing retries and longer completion times.
- Customer reports failed uploads and increased retry costs; visible in their monitoring as elevated 429s between 02:00-04:00 UTC.
- Customer SLA: Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity) — performance degradation is customer-impacting.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: dp-az3-0123 (us-east)
- Service path: api.redwood.example/v1/generate (multipart upload path)
- Platform: prod/us-east with geo-failover to us-west for warmup operations

Steps to reproduce:
1) Schedule a warmup job on the dedicated pool that runs model warmup + kernel profiling (observed on dp-az3-0123).
2) Launch a concurrent multipart backfill: 120 parallel upload workers, each opening streaming sessions and issuing a small number of tokens per chunk.
3) Observe client-side 429s during the overlap window (usually within the first 20 minutes after the warmup rollback completes).

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 429 responses returned from the API gateway for active upload sessions.
- Rate limiter logs show short windows where token accounting is inflated by duplicated warmup probe tokens and queued warmup callbacks.
- Throttling appears shortly after a scheduled rollback that reverts warmup configuration to a previous state.

Expected behavior:
- Warmup operations should not increment tenant-facing token counters or should be accounted separately from customer request quotas. Backfill uploads should be rate-limited by configured per-tenant quotas only, not by internal warmup probes.

Logs / traces:
- API gateway sample: 2026-03-12T02:17:03Z GET /v1/upload 429 token_bucket_exhausted tenant=atlassearch key=key-prod-xx pool=dp-az3-0123
- Rate-limiter trace: warmup_probe=true bucket_charge=10 reason=warmup-callback duplicate_count=3
- Serving runtime metric spike: kv-cache-warmup-count increased 8x during 02:10-02:22 UTC, coincident with the rollback event.

Business impact and customer notes:
- AtlasSearch has a medium-sized backfill that is cost-sensitive; repeated retries push their bill and increase job completion time. Customer asks for an immediate mitigation and a long-term fix.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support temporarily disabled the scheduled rollback on dp-az3-0123 for AtlasSearch scheduled at 02:00 UTC. This reduced 429s in the subsequent window (monitoring shows a drop to baseline within 10 minutes).

Attachments and links:
- Link to customer logs (s3): s3://customer-logs/atlassearch/2026-03-12/warmup-backfill.log
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood/instrumentation/pool/dp-az3-0123/rate-limiter

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: scheduled rollback toggles kernel/profile state which triggers duplicate warmup probes; probes currently run through the same token accounting pipeline as customer requests. Evidence: rate-limiter logs show warmup_probe=true entries and duplicate_count >1 correlated to the rollback window. Checked billing hooks and confirmed no invoice mis-attribution. Reproduced in a staging dedicated pool by forcing a rollback and running parallel multipart upload workers; observed similar short spike in 429s.
Technical checks performed:
- Pulled rate-limiter audit logs for dp-az3-0123 (02:00-03:00 UTC)
- Correlated warmup job IDs with timestamped spikes
- Ran a controlled rollback on staging and reproduced increased bucket charges for warmup probes
- Verified that disabling the rollback eliminated the spike in the customer's environment
resolution_notes:
Short-term: disabled scheduled rollback for AtlasSearch's dedicated pool (dp-az3-0123) and advised customer to reschedule any backfills outside warmup windows. This reduced 429 occurrence to baseline.
Long-term: engineering to deploy change to the rate-limiter so internal warmup probes are accounted on a separate 'system' bucket (excluded from tenant quotas) and add a guard in the scheduler to serialize rollback operations with quota-safe mode. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4231. Target rollout: 2026-03-20 with canary in us-west.
Follow-ups: postmortem and runbook update to avoid warmup rollback during customer backfills; notify AtlasSearch when fix is deployed.
